newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan car imports suffer first drop in 3 years.
newsitem.headline: Japan car imports suffer first drop in 3 years.

text.p: Japan reported a nearly three percent drop in car imports in August, the first fall in nearly three years, as local makers imported fewer cars made at their overseas production plants, an industry body said on Thursday.
"Imports of foreign cars fell mainly because Japanese car makers have reduced overseas production," Kunihiko Ono, vice-chief secretary of the Japan Automobile Importers Association (JAIA) said.
He also said the yen's weakness against the dollar helped reduce car imports.
JAIA said on Thursday that imports of foreign cars dropped 2.9 percent compared to a year earlier to 26,542. It was the first year-on-year drop in 34 months.

It also said imports of cars with engines bigger than 2,000 cc fell 11.3 percent to 15,954 units year-on-year, while imports of cars with smaller engines than that increased 5.6 percent to 7,478 units.
The statistics include automobiles produced by Japanese makers' plants overseas.
A production shift back to Japan was due to local consumers' preference for Japanese cars made in their home country, Ono said.

"Japanese consumers feel that products of Japanese auto makers are Japanese, regardless of the origin of production. However, there exists a psychological factor which leans towards a preference for Japan-made Japanese brand cars rather than foreign-made Japanese brand cars," he added.

Overseas production was especially low in the U.S. manufacturing plants of Honda Motor Co Ltd and Toyota Motor Corp as they started to produce new models of station wagons and recreational vehicles in Japan. These types of cars were not produced in Japan before, the official said.
On the rise in imports of smaller cars, Ono said: "This is because there is a structural shift to the production of inexpensive, energy-saving, environment-friendly vehicles among car makers.
"The trend is especially evident in European auto makers, and even luxury car makers like Mercedes-Benz and BMW are starting to introduce smaller and less expensive models," he added.

Despite the fall in August, Ono said he thinks total imports for 1996 could reach 450,000 units, with consumers buying before the end of the year and before a planned rise in Japan's consumption tax in April.
"It is very difficult to make any projections after April," Ono said.
JAIA said despite the low figures overall, imports from foreign auto makers in August actually remained at the same level, or showed slight an improvement.
